candidates.rule: Shop stars are a percentile among shops, so a buyer's high ratings can lift competitors.
candidates.quote: shop stars are a percentile among shops, so our buyer's 5s lift the competitors
candidates.harness: Treat shop stars as a relative percentile and account for the competitive effect of buyer ratings.

candidates.rule: On 2026-11-04, the user chose price-only reviews: give 5 stars at 60% of value or less for any grade, one star less than the base 4 above 90% of value, and 1 star for a false claim, higher receipt, or worthless item; do not deduct for grade.
candidates.quote: user 11/4 13:5x: do not split by grade
candidates.harness: Use the price-only thresholds and penalties; do not apply a grade-based deduction.

candidates.rule: The stock cap is based on a share of equity, defined as balance plus stock at cost; buying stock preserves equity and does not shrink the cap.
candidates.harness: Calculate the stock cap from balance plus stock at cost, rather than from the starting balance.

candidates.rule: At a 15.7M balance, the old stock cap left 2.1M available for buying while 9.0M cash was free, and 35 of 86 visits in 30 minutes found no stock.
candidates.quote: at 15.7M balance it left 2.1M to buy while 9.0M of cash was free, and 35 of 86 visits in 30 min found no stock
candidates.harness: Monitor available buying capacity and stockouts when balance grows; the old starting-cap basis caused understocking.

candidates.rule: Restock goods using 1.5 times each SKU's combined units sold and units visitors asked for but could not find during the previous two hours.
candidates.quote: demand per SKU = what we sold + what visitors asked for and found missing, both in 2 h, x1.5
candidates.harness: Measure both sales and missed demand over two hours and use 1.5 times their sum to set goods restock depth.

candidates.rule: Food restocking grows with measured demand, up to 10 units per SKU.
candidates.quote: food grows with it up to 10 a SKU
candidates.harness: Scale food orders with measured demand and cap each food SKU at 10 units.

candidates.rule: Allocate restock money first to SKUs with the greatest demand, then use value as the tie-breaker.
candidates.quote: The money goes first to the SKUs with the most demand, then value
candidates.harness: Rank buy-list items by demand first and value second before allocating limited funds.

candidates.rule: On 2026-11-04, water SKU G7fa48eaa had 20 missed requests but received only one unit because it ranked behind a 2.2M sofa; the revised allocation raised its order to nine.
candidates.quote: water G7fa48eaa, asked 20 times, came last behind a 2.2M sofa and got 1 unit; now its 9
candidates.harness: Avoid letting high-priced goods displace high-demand essentials when allocating restock funds.

candidates.rule: At 17:1x on 2026-11-04, the user asked whether the shop should spend more and how; free cash was 17.93M, all planned each window, 33 buy-list lines were omitted for lack of cash, and 43 of 847 orders were refunded.
candidates.quote: user question for the strategy agent (11/4 17:1x: the cash is large, should we spend more and how?)
candidates.harness: Treat the spending policy as an open strategy question rather than assuming that free cash should be spent without limits.

candidates.rule: The restock cost share sets expected unit cost for the buy list, stock cap, cash floor, and warranty reserve; the 75%-of-list worst-case cost must still preserve the plain cash floor, and unaffordable plans are cut rather than refused.
candidates.quote: the worst cost (75% of list) still has to keep the plain cash floor, in check.buy and in act.allocate, so a plan is cut rather than refused
candidates.harness: Budget against the 75%-of-list worst case, preserve the cash floor in both checks and allocation, and trim plans that exceed the budget.

candidates.rule: The user approved option A on 2026-11-04: use a 0.65 restock cost share and a 6% warranty reserve.
candidates.harness: Use a restock cost share of 0.65 and reserve 6% for warranty.

candidates.rule: At 19:47 on 2026-11-04, the shop had a 23,194,111 balance, a 14,535,724 warranty reserve for 432 goods sales worth 242M still under warranty, 8,158,387 available to plan, and a binding stock cap of 4,897,566.
candidates.harness: Track warranty liabilities and the binding stock cap when calculating spendable funds.

candidates.rule: On 2026-11-04, the user selected food-buying option A+B: open bids at 55%, aim for 68%, cap at 82%, allow 30 seconds per food order, 8 seconds per message, and 12 shops.
candidates.harness: Apply the chosen food bid levels and the 30-second order, 8-second message, and 12-shop limits.

candidates.rule: Over six hours, lee-sungsoo closed 62% of food orders at a median 69% of list, while this shop closed 34% at 54%; this shop had 1,258 of 2,321 shop talks rejected and 214 timeouts.
candidates.quote: lee-sungsoo (buyer ALL 0.733, food 87%) closes 62% of orders at a median 69% of list, we close 34% at 54%
candidates.harness: Use the observed competitor performance as a benchmark, while retaining that the competitor's round-3 code was not public.

candidates.rule: In a six-hour measurement, shop talks ended in 1–2 seconds, and sequential tries lost a median 4.6 seconds on 197 of 554 won food orders.
candidates.quote: shop talks end in 1-2 s and sequential tries lose a median 4.6 s on 197 of 554 won food orders
candidates.harness: Account for the time cost of sequential food-shop probing when designing buyer order behavior.

candidates.rule: In a six-hour measurement, 343 of 1,058 food receipts were unpaid because of short shelf life; grade-C receipts for orders longer than 45% of shelf life were refused 138 of 146 times, so the shelf-life guard should run first.
candidates.quote: a receipt claiming grade C for an order longer than 45% of the shelf was refused 138 of 146 times, so the guard goes first
candidates.harness: Check the order duration against 45% of shelf life before accepting a grade-C receipt.

candidates.rule: Buyer parallel probing and a shelf-life guard were described as a draft on 2026-11-04, not as live behavior.
candidates.harness: Do not assume parallel probing or the shelf-life guard is already active; treat it as a proposed design until deployed.

candidates.rule: When a schema change requires a restart, restart the seller and outer processes so they use the new schema.
candidates.quote: seller and outer restarted for the schema
candidates.harness: Restart both seller and outer processes after applicable schema changes.
